narrative: During the 1940s, Black and African women's hairstyles and hair culture were deeply rooted in their rich heritage and traditions. While specific details about hairstyles during this era are limited in our source material, we can infer that protective styles, such as braids and twists, were likely popular due to the need to minimize manipulation and exposure of Afro-textured hair to environmental elements. Cornrows, a traditional African hairstyle, may have been worn by women during this time, as they are still considered an important part of African braiding practice today. The natural texture and beauty of Black and African hair was undoubtedly celebrated, with many women embracing their unique kinks and curls. Unfortunately, our source material does not provide more specific information about hairstyles in the 1940s, but it is clear that hair culture played a significant role in the lives of Black and African women during this era.
